title: 0.5 Lists
objectives: Build a list from nothing with [] and append(), and read items back with positive and negative indexes
Slice a list, use len() and `in`, and explain why the last valid index is len - 1 (and what IndexError means)
Guard an index with a length check so a cut-off serial line can't crash your parser
Explain list aliasing (two names, one list) and make a real copy with [:] when you need one
Loop over a list with for and enumerate, and find the max/min of a list of readings

predict.question: A sentence was cut off mid-transmission. What does this print?
predict.why: len(fields) is 3, so the valid indexes are 0, 1, and 2. Index 3 is one past the end, so Python raises IndexError. The last item is fields[len(fields) - 1], or simply fields[-1]. This is the classic off-by-one: the length counts items starting from 1, indexes start from 0.

predict.question: You make a 'backup' of your altitude window, then add a reading through the backup. What does this print?
predict.why: backup = window does NOT copy anything. It gives the same list a second name, like two wires landed on the same terminal. Appending through either name changes the one list, so window sees 12.8 too. To get an independent copy, write backup = window[:]. (append adds to the END, which is why it isn't [12.8, 12.3, 13.0].)

predict.question: split() gives you a list of strings. What does this print?
predict.code:
fields = "$GPGGA,152305.00,4220.1234,N,07105.5678,W,1,09".split(",")
print(9 in fields, "09" in fields, "GGA" in fields)
predict.why: `in` on a list compares whole items with ==. The items are strings, so the number 9 never equals the text '09' (False), while '09' matches exactly (True). 'GGA' is only PART of the item '$GPGGA', and a list doesn't search inside its items, so that's False too. (On a string, `in` does search for text inside it, which is why "GGA" in line works on the whole line.)

visualizations.title: Trace: two names, one list

props.code:
log = [12.3, 13.0]
backup = log
safe = log[:]
log.append(12.8)
print(backup)
print(safe)
print(backup is log, safe is log)

visualizations.notice: After log.append(12.8), BOTH log and backup change in the variables table, because they are the same list. safe was built by log[:] before the append, so it's a separate list and stays [12.3, 13.0].

predictFirst.question: Before you trace: after log.append(12.8), what will backup and safe each hold? Will backup is log be True? Will safe is log?
predictFirst.reveal: backup is [12.3, 13.0, 12.8]: it's just another name for log. safe is [12.3, 13.0]: log[:] built a NEW list before the append. So backup is log is True, and safe is log is False.

visualizations.title: Trace: find the worst HDOP with enumerate

props.code:
hdops = [1.1, 2.8, 1.4, 1.0]
worst = hdops[0]
worst_i = 0
for i, h in enumerate(hdops):
    if h > worst:
        worst = h
        worst_i = i
print("worst fix:", worst_i, "HDOP", worst)
print("check:", max(hdops))

visualizations.notice: Watch i and h change together on every pass: enumerate hands you the position AND the item. worst only changes when a bigger value shows up. max() gives the same answer in one call, but only the loop tells you WHERE the worst fix was.

challenge.task: Write satellite_counts(sentences), which returns a list of int satellite counts from the GGA sentences in a list of NMEA lines (skipping other types, cut-off lines, and empty satellite fields), and last_n(readings, n), which returns a new list with the newest n readings without changing the input.

bug.bugType: list aliasing (a buffer changed through a second name)
bug.report: Post-run report from the field team: "The altitude plot looks great, but the saved raw log is wrong. The 87.4 m multipath spike we saw live is missing from the raw data. It shows 20.0 m, the plot ceiling." clamped() is supposed to return a clamped copy for plotting and leave the raw log untouched. Find the bug and fix it.

explainBack.prompt: In your own words: why did result = altitudes let clamped() damage the raw log, and how does altitudes[:] fix it? And why must satellite_counts check the length of the field list before reading fields[7]?
rubric: Explains that assignment gives a second name to the SAME list (no copy is made), so a change through either name shows up through both
Explains that a full slice [:] builds a new, separate list, so changing the copy leaves the original alone
Explains that a cut-off sentence has fewer fields, so fields[7] would raise IndexError; the last valid index is len - 1, so the list needs more than 7 items

challenge: Two separate jobs. For satellite_counts: which index is the satellites field, and what must be true about the field list before you're allowed to read that index? For last_n: which slice gives the END of a list, and what number is -0?

satellite_counts: start with an empty list, loop over the sentences, strip and split each one, and keep it only if it is a GGA sentence, its field list has MORE than 7 items, and field 7 isn't empty. Convert field 7 to a number before appending. last_n: a negative slice gives the newest n items and is always a new list, but n == 0 needs its own case, because -0 is just 0 and [0:] is the whole list.

satellite_counts: counts = empty list; for each line in sentences: fields = split(strip(line), ','); if characters 3 to 6 of fields[0] are 'GGA' AND length of fields > 7 AND fields[7] is not empty: append int(fields[7]) to counts. return counts. last_n: if n is 0 or less: return an empty list; otherwise return readings sliced from -n to the end.
bug: After the line result = altitudes runs, how many lists exist? Two, or one list with two names? Try printing result is altitudes.
Make result a real copy (a full slice) BEFORE the loop changes anything. Then the assignments inside the loop go into the copy, and the raw log is never touched.
